run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} on index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned 0 hits. The index mapping has no `level` field at all: its only mapped properties are @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword), so severity is stored as the integer field severity_num and as bracketed prefixes inside the msg text. Re-running against severity_num with [5,6] returned 8 hits (severity_num=5 → 6 documents, severity_num=6 → 2 documents), and an independent full-text check on msg for ERROR/FATAL also returned 8 hits, so the two representations agree. The whole index holds 23 documents, all with svc=order-276, within the tool's applied @timestamp window 2026-11-23T17:10:15Z–2026-11-23T18:10:15Z (document timestamps 18:05:01Z–18:08:10Z): INFO(3)=10, WARN(4)=5, ERROR(5)=6, FATAL(6)=2. The number-to-name correspondence (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL) comes from the msg text, since the mapping carries no severity code table. No fault or root cause was investigated here; this is a counting exercise only.

claims.text: The query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} against index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned total value 0 (relation eq), with the @timestamp filter applied over 2026-11-23T17:10:15Z to 2026-11-23T18:10:15Z.

The mapping of app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m contains only the properties @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); there is no `level` property, which explains the zero-hit terms query on level.
The severity field is severity_num: {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}} returned 8 hits, with aggregation buckets severity_num=5 doc_count 6 and severity_num=6 doc_count 2.
Cross-check on the text field: a bool/should match on msg for "ERROR" or "FATAL" returned the same 8 hits, independently confirming the count of 8 error/fatal records.
Unfiltered aggregation over the index window: 23 documents in total, all svc=order-276, distributed as severity_num=3 (10 docs), 4 (5 docs), 5 (6 docs) and 6 (2 docs).

The stored documents show the label-to-number correspondence: msgs "[ERROR] DB timeout 1"–"[ERROR] DB timeout 6" carry severity_num 5, "[FATAL] Disk full 1"–"[FATAL] Disk full 2" carry severity_num 6, "[WARN] Slow query" carries 4 and "[INFO] Order placed" carries 3; document @timestamp range was 2026-11-23T18:05:01Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:10Z.

Because ERROR/FATAL lines cluster in msg prefixes and severity_num 5/6 while every document is from svc=order-276, the 8 error/fatal records plausibly describe a DB-timeout and disk-full condition in the order-276 application; this is not verified here since no other signal for that service was examined.
Query log severity on severity_num (5 for ERROR, 6 for FATAL) or on the msg text field rather than a nonexistent `level` field, and avoid field names not present in the index mapping.

gaps: The elasticsearch tool forces an @timestamp filter (here 2026-11-23T17:10:15Z–2026-11-23T18:10:15Z); counts apply only to that window, not to the index's whole history. The 23-document index total and the 8-hit count coincide only because all stored documents fall inside that one-hour window.

The index mapping defines no severity code table or description field, so the mapping of severity_num 5→ERROR and 6→FATAL is inferred from msg prefixes in the returned documents, not from schema metadata.
Any log records written after 2026-11-23T18:10:15Z, or dropped by retention, are unknown; zero hits for the `level` field name would also be the result for an unmapped field regardless of content.
No Prometheus, trace or Kubernetes signals were examined, so the cause of the order-276 ERROR/FATAL lines is not established.
next_steps: If the error condition matters, query severity_num>=5 over a wider period and correlate with order-276 service metrics/traces and pod logs.
